source: Aswath Damodaran, Valuation lecture packet 1 (Spring 2020 / Spring 2021), NYU Stern. Altman cumulative-default mapping via apv.xls; startup survival from the 2007 study reproduced in the packet; long-run sector survival from US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Business Employment Dynamics, 1994-2019 cohorts.
refresh: Default rates are re-estimated annually. Refresh rating_cumulative_default_10y from Altman's current mortality tables or S&P's Annual Global Corporate Default Study, and sector_long_run_survival from the BLS Business Employment Dynamics release. Record the vintage in the valuation. Pass a refreshed file with reference_path rather than editing this copy.

rating_cumulative_default_10y.note: Cumulative likelihood that a bond in this rating class defaults within ten years. Estimated by taking the bonds in each class ten years earlier and measuring the proportion that defaulted. Ratings are S&P letter grades.

B+.note: The Las Vegas Sands case (February 2009) quotes 28.25% for B+ from the S&P study of that year rather than 25.00% from the Altman mapping. Rating-implied probabilities move with the vintage; state which one you used.

startup_survival_by_year.note: Share of firms started in a given year that are still alive n years later, all sectors, read from the 2007 study chart in the packet. Use one minus the survival rate as the probability of failure over that horizon for a company with no debt to price.

sector_long_run_survival.note: Share of businesses started in 1994 still operating in 2019. Long-run survival differs by a factor of three across sectors, so an all-firm average is a poor default when the sector is known.

conventions.recovery_note: Distress proceeds default to 50% of the chosen base, the value used in Damodaran's Ginzu model and in the JC Penney case. Cut it in an economy-wide downturn, when every peer is selling the same assets at once.
conventions.bond_model_note: The bond-implied probability assumes zero recovery in distress and discounts the promised payments at the riskfree rate. Both are modelling choices. A non-zero recovery assumption lowers the implied probability for the same price.
